name: How do I design an addition for a corner lot home?

mainEntity.name: What changes when the house sits on a corner lot instead of a standard lot?
mainEntity.text: What changes when the house sits on a corner lot instead of a standard lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Corner lots give homeowners more design freedom in some ways and more scrutiny in others. Because the home is visible from two streets, an addition must be planned from more than one angle. That means the side elevation often matters as much as the front. Setbacks and privacy considerations can also be different from those on a standard interior lot, which affects where the addition can be placed. A poor design can make the house feel bulky or expose too much of the new volume to public view. A strong design uses the extra visibility to its advantage by shaping a balanced exterior, aligning rooflines carefully, and placing windows where they add light without sacrificing privacy. For homes in Los Angeles or Pasadena corner-lot neighborhoods, the addition should feel intentional from every street-facing side.
acceptedAnswer.description: Corner lots usually create more visibility, more setback constraints, and more attention to street-facing design. That means the addition must work from multiple angles, not just the rear. Window placement, massing, and rooflines matter more because neighbors and passersby can see more of the home.
